profile.name: Singo Ulung
profile.tagline: A traditional lion dance from the Bondowoso regency of East Java, Indonesia.
profile.insight: Created by the first head of Blimbing village, Mbah Singo Wulu, this lion dance uses costumes crafted from decomposed raffia string to honor the village's founding spirit.
profile.profile: Singo Ulung is a traditional dance from Bondowoso, East Java, performed by two dancers inside a lion-shaped costume. It serves as a central ritual for the annual Bersih Desa purification ceremony in Blimbing village. The performance, which also features characters like Panji and warok dancers, is a key cultural marker of the region's history.
profile.profile_long: Singo Ulung is a traditional dance originating from the Bondowoso regency in East Java, Indonesia. The dance is performed by two individuals who operate a singular lion-like costume, known as the 'Singo'. This costume is distinct from other lion dances, such as the Barongsai, due to its construction; it is made from raffia string that has been decomposed until it achieves a fur-like texture. The color palette of the costume typically features plain white, or combinations of black and white, or yellow and white. The performers inside the costume wear simple training pants and T-shirts, emphasizing the focus on the movement of the lion figure itself. The dance is deeply rooted in the history of Blimbing village in the Klabang district. According to local tradition, the dance was created by Mbah Singo Wulu, the first head of Blimbing village, who moved to the area from Ponorogo. Mbah Singo Wulu and his wife, Nyi Moena, alongside Ki Jasiman, were instrumental in fostering the prosperity of the village, and the dance serves as a tribute to this founding legacy. The performance is not a solitary act; it is part of a broader ensemble that includes characters such as Panji and Jasiman, who wear costumes similar to those found in Tari Topeng. Female dancers participate in traditional kebaya and sampur, while warok dancers, dressed in all-black outfits with Madhure red-white shirts, carry cemethi as attributes for their performance. The dance is a central component of the annual Bersih Desa, a village purification ritual held in the month of Sya'ban or Ruwah. During this ceremony, the community honors the rice goddess Sri, the village's tutelary spirit, and the founding figures of the village. Beyond the ritual context, Singo Ulung is performed during the anniversary of the Bondowoso regency on August 16th, as well as at festivals and for welcoming guests. The preservation of this art form is currently managed by various local art galleries, ensuring that the tradition remains a living part of Bondowoso's cultural identity.

sections.origins_and_history: The dance was created by Mbah Singo Wulu, the first head of Blimbing village in Bondowoso, who migrated from Ponorogo. It is performed to honor the village's founding spirit and is intrinsically linked to the annual Bersih Desa purification ritual.
sections.how_it_is_danced: Two dancers operate the lion costume together, mimicking the movements of a lion. The performance includes additional characters such as Panji, Jasiman, female dancers in kebaya, and warok dancers who carry whips (cemethi).
sections.music_and_instruments: The dance is accompanied by music intended to astonish the audience. Specific instruments are not described in sources.
sections.costume_and_setting: The lion costume is made of decomposed raffia string. Panji and Jasiman wear Tari Topeng-style costumes. Female dancers wear kebaya and sampur. Warok dancers wear black with red-white shirts and carry whips.
sections.occasions_and_meaning: It is performed annually during the Bersih Desa ritual in Blimbing village (month of Sya'ban) and on the anniversary of Bondowoso (August 16). It is considered a main ritual means that cannot be replaced.
sections.notable_figures: Mbah Singo Wulu (creator and first head of Blimbing village), Nyi Moena, and Ki Jasiman.

profile.sacred_note: The dance is a central, irreplaceable component of the Bersih Desa village purification ritual and is treated with cultural reverence.

claims.text: Singo Ulung is a traditional dance from Bondowoso regency, East Java, played by two people in a lion-like costume.
claims.quote: Singo Ulung (Javanese: ꦱꦶꦔꦲꦸꦭꦸꦁ, romanized: Singa Ulung, Javanese pronunciation: [siːŋɔ ʊlʊŋ]) is one of the original traditional dances from Bondowoso regency, East Java, Indonesia. The dance is played by two people in a lion-like costume

claims.text: The costume is made of raffia string that has been decomposed to look like fur.
claims.quote: The material of the costume is raffia string, decomposed until it looks like fur.

claims.text: The dance was created by Mbah Singo Wulu, the first head of Blimbing village.
claims.quote: That's why he was chosen to become the first head of Blimbing village. One day, he had an idea to create a public traditional dance called Singo Ulung

claims.text: The dance is performed during the annual Bersih Desa purification ceremony in Blimbing village.
claims.quote: Elle est exécutée à Blimbing lors de la cérémonie annuelle du bersih desa, rite de purification du village

claims.text: The dance is also performed on the anniversary of Bondowoso on August 16.
claims.quote: Singo ulung est également exécutée lors des fêtes pour l'anniversaire de la fondation de Bondowoso, le 16 août.

claims.text: The dance is considered a main ritual means for the village ceremony and cannot be replaced.
claims.quote: It is necessary to perform Singo Ulung in the ritual village ceremony because it is considered a main means and cannot be replaced by others.

claims.text: The dance is still being preserved and studied by several art galleries.
claims.quote: The Singo Ulung dance is still being preserved and studied by several art galleries there.
